title: Call yourself
prompt:
Write `fact`, a subroutine that computes a factorial by calling itself, and use it to print `10!`.

 Each call to `fact` needs its own frame (`lr` must survive the recursive `bl`), and `n` has to outlive the recursive call, which means a callee-saved register that you save on entry and restore on exit. Base case first: when `n` is 1 or less, the answer is 1. Otherwise it is `n * fact(n - 1)`.

## what is checked

- `10!` printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- a real call chain does it: a frame is built (`stp`) and the recursion happens (`bl`), with no precomputed answer
starter:
// compute a factorial with a recursive subroutine
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(n_r, x19)

        .data
fmt:    .string "10! = %lld\n"

        .text

// fact(x0 = n) -> x0 = n!
        .balign 4
        .global fact
fact:
        // TODO: the base case returns 1 when n is 1 or less.
        // Otherwise save what must survive (this function calls
        // itself, so lr needs a frame, and n needs to live in a
        // callee-saved register that you save and restore), recurse on
        // n - 1, and multiply the result by n on the way back up.
        mov     x0, 1                       // replace this placeholder
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     x0, 10                      // the argument
        bl      fact

        mov     x1, x0
        ldr     x0, =fmt
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
